documents.title: Common Rust: overview
documents.content: Common rust is a fungal leaf disease of maize; severe infections can injure leaves.

documents.title: Common Rust: symptoms
documents.content: Elongated cinnamon-brown pustules occur on both leaf surfaces and darken with age. Severe infection may yellow or kill leaves; distinguish other rusts through examination.

documents.title: Common Rust: causes
documents.content: The rust fungus Puccinia sorghi causes common rust. Wind carries infectious spores.

documents.title: Common Rust: conditions
documents.content: Cool, damp weather, heavy dew, high humidity and sustained leaf wetness favor common rust. Young leaves are particularly susceptible.

documents.title: Gray Leaf Spot: overview
documents.content: Gray leaf spot is a fungal maize leaf disease; its importance depends on local growing conditions.

documents.title: Gray Leaf Spot: symptoms
documents.content: Small dead spots with halos enlarge into gray or brown rectangular lesions, usually bordered by leaf veins. Other leaf diseases can look similar.

documents.title: Gray Leaf Spot: causes
documents.content: The cited source identifies Cercospora zeae-maydis and notes survival in maize residue on the soil surface.

documents.title: Gray Leaf Spot: conditions
documents.content: Prolonged humid or wet weather with moderate to warm temperatures favors infection. Continuous maize and retained infected residue can increase risk.

documents.title: Northern Corn Leaf Blight: overview
documents.content: Northern corn leaf blight damages maize foliage. Early infection can threaten grain yield in susceptible hybrids.

source.title: Northern corn leaf blight

documents.title: Northern Corn Leaf Blight: symptoms
documents.content: Long canoe-shaped lesions start with gray-green margins and become tan, sometimes with dark fungal growth. Symptoms often progress from lower to upper leaves; other diseases can resemble them.

documents.title: Northern Corn Leaf Blight: causes
documents.content: Exserohilum turcicum causes this disease and survives on maize leaf debris. Pathogen races interact differently with hybrid resistance genes.

documents.title: Northern Corn Leaf Blight: conditions
documents.content: Moderate temperatures and prolonged moisture favor disease. Infections established before silking can be more damaging.

documents.content: Scouting starts by recognizing normal plant growth and detecting deviations. The source concerns early-season field assessment, not an image classifier's definition of Healthy.

documents.title: Healthy / scouting context: symptoms
documents.content: During early-season scouting, check for yellowing, wilting, stunting, dead or missing plants, and discolored or decaying maize roots or mesocotyls. These observations warrant investigation, not an automatic disease diagnosis.

documents.title: Healthy / scouting context: prevention
documents.content: Record crop growth stage and seek an agronomist's help when problems are unclear. Laboratory examination may be needed to identify a seedling pathogen.
